issues.description: Tests substitute additions=[] with a bogus zero-amount/zero-puzhash Addition to satisfy the non-empty-list guard.
issues.detail: The test was bent to fit the new code path rather than the reverse: a phantom Addition is injected to pass CreateSignedTransaction's len(additions)>=1 check. This signals the wrapped data model does not actually fit the cat_spend call when request.additions is None. Fix the model so the production caller can produce what the validator requires, then restore honest tests.

issues.description: send_transaction silently changes puzzle_decorator semantics, no longer slicing to index 0.
issues.detail: Old code forwarded only request.puzzle_decorator[0]; the new path forwards the whole list, and _generate_signed_transaction iterates all of them. Meanwhile cat_spend drops puzzle_decorator entirely. Two endpoints, two divergent silent semantic changes. Pick one contract, document it, and honor it across both call sites.

issues.description: Address-prefix validation silently switched from network-config prefix check to AddressType.XCH allowed set.
issues.detail: Old send_transaction rejected on bech32 prefix mismatch against the network config's address_prefix. New code uses ensure_valid_address with allowed_types={AddressType.XCH} — enum membership, not config string compare. On testnet/simulator builds where the configured prefix is not xch this is a behavior change and possible regression. Pin the equivalence with a test or restore the original check.

issues.description: CreateSignedTransaction becomes a junk drawer of CAT- and decorator-specific optional fields from two unrelated endpoints.
issues.detail: Adding extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution, and puzzle_decorator onto the general request type pushes CAT-specific state into a structure that no longer describes one thing. Extract a CatDiscrepancy value object owned in one place and passed through, so both endpoints and the shared transaction-building core consume one honest shape instead of syncing two classes by convention.

issues.description: get_wallet is called purely for its raising side effect, annotated only by a comment.
issues.detail: The pattern '# opportunity to raise' followed by a discarded call is a smuggled assertion. The precondition that the wallet exists and has the required type is now enforced by an unnamed side effect whose return is thrown away. Expose a named validate_wallet(id, type) helper so the contract is explicit instead of folkloric.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation carries forward its `None in {set}` trick and three type: ignore suppressions unchanged.
issues.detail: The extracted helper preserves bad taste rather than fixing it: a set-membership None check across mixed bytes/str types plus three # type: ignore[arg-type] comments. An explicit `if extra_delta is None or tail_reveal is None or tail_solution is None` narrows for mypy, deletes the ignores, and reads off the page. Extracting code without strengthening its spec is mere motion.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the deduplication direction is right — send_transaction and cat_spend as thin wrappers over create_signed_transaction is the correct shape — but execution leaks observable behavior changes. The loudest tell is the test diff inventing a zero-amount/zero-puzhash Addition to satisfy a non-empty-list invariant, proving the wrapped data model does not fit the caller. puzzle_decorator handling diverges silently between the two endpoints, and address-prefix validation switched semantics without justification. CreateSignedTransaction has become a junk drawer of CAT- and decorator-specific optional fields; the extracted cat_discrepancy_validation helper carries old type-ignores forward. Needs work before merge.
